notes: Sub-plan created: identifier STP-6 (confirms the declared STP-NNN format), numeric plan id 48284 recoverable only from urls.self (https://test-management-preprod.bsstag.com/projects/379335744/test-plans/48284) — matches the pattern seen on TP-1616 (48283), i.e. no numeric id field in the payload. parent_plan_id CLOSES THE OPEN QUESTION: it is populated on the create response itself (value 'TP-1616', the parent's TP-NNN identifier — not its numeric id 48283), and remains populated identically on an independent get_test_plan read-back of STP-6 (again 'TP-1616'). So the nested schema's claim ('present only when this plan is a sub-plan') is correct in substance and, on this real sub-plan, is populated with the identifier form as documented — good news for that thread. However, the sibling's observation that the flat `returns` array lists parent_plan_id unconditionally (i.e. without the sub-plan caveat) still stands as a separate, lesser drift on the flat array's completeness, since on a top-level plan (TP-1616 itself) parent_plan_id is genuinely absent (not present-but-null) per the parent-plan probe. sub_plans_count on TP-1616 went 0 -> 1 after the sub-plan was created, confirmed via an independent get_test_plan re-read (not just the create echo) — the child is real, not drift. On the sub-plan itself (STP-6), sub_plans_count came back as the integer 0, not null, contradicting the nested schema's explicit claim ('sub_plans_count ... null on a sub-plan') — recorded as drift; the value is well-formed (an empty-children plan reporting 0) but the documented null-on-sub-plan behavior did not hold. list_test_plans (count=300, single page, info.count=2) returned only the project's two top-level plans (TP-1616, TP-1596) and did NOT include STP-6 — sub-plans do NOT appear in this listing; must use the per-parent sub-plan listing/read instead, consistent with list_test_plans's own guidance ('list a parent's children through the sub-plans listing'). Depth limit for nesting a sub-plan under a sub-plan was NOT tested destructively per instructions: create_sub_test_plan's own path_param regex for test_plan_id is ^(TP|STP)-\d+$ (would route-match an STP-NNN parent too), but its prose describes the parent strictly as 'TP-NNN' and states a created sub-plan itself 'cannot be re-parented or promoted afterwards on v2' — the contract gives no explicit statement either way on whether STP-under-STP nesting is accepted or rejected server-side, so this remains an open question, not something inferred from an actual call. Guidance's request-shape trap (recommending a `sub_test_plan` wrapper that invokeCapability itself rejects) matches the pattern already seen on create_test_plan in this suite — same class of drift, different capability. No 4xx/5xx HTTP responses were encountered in this probe (the one rejection was client-side, before any HTTP call), so the error-envelope-honoured question does not apply here.
